title: Morphisms out of a dense compactification
statement:
Let $X,S$ be schemes and $f:X\to S$ a morphism. Let
$c'=(X\xrightarrow{j'}\overline X'\xrightarrow{p'}S)$ be a dense
compactification [def-nagata-dense-compactification] and
$c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S)$ a compactification
[def-nagata-compactification] of $f$. Assume explicitly that both open
immersions $j,j'$ are quasi-compact: their inverse images of affine open
subschemes are quasi-compact topological spaces. Thus these are the
compactifications to which [det-nagata-definition-refinement] applies.
Let $h:\overline X'\to\overline X$ be an $S$-morphism, meaning
$p\circ h=p'$, with $h\circ j'=j$. Then:

1. $h$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism];
2. $h^{-1}(j(X))=j'(X)$ as open subschemes of $\overline X'$, so $h$ is
   a refinement $c'\to c$ [det-nagata-definition-refinement];
3. $h$ is the unique $S$-morphism $\overline X'\to\overline X$ with
   $h\circ j'=j$.

proof.text: Properness. The two compactifications give proper structure maps $p'$ and $p$ by [def-nagata-compactification]. In particular $p$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] to the triangle $\overline X'\xrightarrow{h}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$, whose composite is $p'$. Its source is proper over $S$ and its target is separated over $S$, so $h$ is proper. This packages exactly the graph factorization of the blueprint's first paragraph (Stacks Tag 01W6).

source.place: Proof, Properness; Stacks morphisms.tex, Tag 01W6 (lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed), part (2)

proof.text: Form the open subscheme $V=h^{-1}(j(X))$ of $\overline X'$ and write $i:V\hookrightarrow\overline X'$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $j$ identifies $X$ with its open image. Thus the fibre product $\overline X'\times_{\overline X}X$ is $V$, with second projection $g=j^{-1}\circ h|_V:V\to X$ [def-pc-base-change]. Since $h$ is proper by Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] makes $g$ proper; it is therefore separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The equality $hj'=j$ defines a map $s:X\to V$ with $is=j'$ and $gs=\mathrm{id}_X$: the second equality follows by applying the inverse of the isomorphism $X\simeq j(X)$ to $hj'=j$.

source.place: Proof, Inverse image of X, construction of V and g; Stacks morphisms.tex, Tag 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper)

proof.text: The map $s$ of Step 2 is a section of the separated morphism $g$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] makes $s$ a closed immersion. Its image is exactly $j'(X)$, viewed inside $V$, since $is=j'$. This image is closed by [def-weil-closed-immersion] and open because $j'$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Consequently the complement $V''=V\setminus j'(X)$ is open in $V$, and hence open in $\overline X'$. No assertion that an arbitrary morphism factors through a locally closed subscheme merely from its pointwise image is used: $s$ was constructed through an open subscheme in Step 2.

source.place: Proof, Inverse image of X, section is closed; Stacks schemes.tex, Tag 01KT (lemma-section-immersion)

proof.text: By [def-nagata-dense-compactification] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open], quasi-compactness of $j'$ identifies its density with injectivity of $\mathcal O_{\overline X'}\to j'_*\mathcal O_X$. Restrict this injective sheaf map to the open $V''$ from Step 3. For every open $W\subseteq V''$ its target has sections $\mathcal O_X((j')^{-1}W)=\mathcal O_X(\varnothing)=0$, since $W\cap j'(X)=\varnothing$. Thus $\mathcal O_{V''}=0$. Any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $V''$ then has $A=0$, so has no prime ideals and is empty. Such affine opens cover $V''$, giving $V''=\varnothing$. Therefore $V=j'(X)$. These opens carry the restrictions of the same structure sheaf of $\overline X'$, so this is equality of open subschemes, not only of point sets. Together with the two given commutativities and the quasi-compactness hypotheses, it is precisely a refinement in [det-nagata-definition-refinement].

source.place: Proof, Inverse image of X, restriction to V double-prime and vanishing; Stacks morphisms.tex, Tags 01RD (lemma-scheme-theoretically-dense-quasi-compact) and 01RE (lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense)

proof.text: Let $h_1,h_2:\overline X'\to\overline X$ be any two $S$-morphisms with $h_1j'=j=h_2j'$. Both composites with $p$ equal $p'$. The map $p$ is separated because it is proper [def-nagata-compactification, def-weil-proper-morphism], and $j'$ is scheme-theoretically dominant by the density hypothesis [def-nagata-dense-compactification]. Apply [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] with $s=p$, $T=\overline X'$, $W=X$, and $\iota=j'$: its equality over the base and its equality after $\iota$ are exactly the two displayed identities. It gives $h_1=h_2$. The originally supplied $h$ is one such map, so it is unique.

lean.statement: theorem denseCompactification_refinement_morphisms {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} (c' c : Compactification.QuasiCompactObjects f) (hc' : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant c'.obj.i) (h : c'.obj.Z ⟶ c.obj.Z) (hS : h ≫ c.obj.g = c'.obj.g) (hj : c'.obj.i ≫ h = c.obj.i) : IsProper h ∧ Compactification.boundaryRefinementProperty f (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := c') (Y := c) ⟨h, hj, hS⟩) ∧ ∀ (h' : c'.obj.Z ⟶ c.obj.Z), h' ≫ c.obj.g = c'.obj.g → c'.obj.i ≫ h' = c.obj.i → h' = h
lean.note: Uses QuasiCompactObjects to retain both explicit quasi-compact open immersions; the middle conjunct is the recorded boundaryRefinementProperty, definitionally equality of inverse-image opens. Uniqueness quantifies over arbitrary ambient scheme morphisms satisfying the two triangles.
